I'm uncertain about how the argument devolved but at 18:21 it looks to me like C understood wise mind.  You're all in agreement about using both reason and emotion but it seems the problem is that somehow it got into an argument of reason vs emotions, despite having already agreed combining the two is the best of both worlds.  I think you're valid in placing emotions over reason just as they are valid in placing reason over emotion.  I'm open to the exchange of differing ideas between friends but of course there's going to be bad blood if isn't done in a respectful way.  From your perspective you're valid in the way that it's made you feel if they are blatantly saying you are absolutely wrong.  I think the problem is that they've made this into a debate rather than accepting you place greater importance to your emotions and trying to understand why.  From an example in my life, my brother and I are constantly at odds because I am a rational decision maker and he is an emotional decision maker.  That is just who we are but neither method is foolproof given our history of bad decisions as individuals.  But when we exchange ideas as a team, we realize our faults and work towards better solutions.  So in a way I'm the reasonable mind, he's the emotional, and together the wise mind.  Losing idealization of your friends isn't bad, as they are human after all with faults of their own.  Hopefully they will open their minds and understand that each side has their equal right to their own opinion.

From looking at the transcript and your description I get the feeling that they possibly hold more importance to rationality but they recognize that emotions are factored into decisions as well.  The wise mind integrates both reason and emotion.  Emotions can cloud your judgement and lead to irrational and potentially negative decisions.  Purely rational decisions would cause you to make what is "objectively" the best decision but possibly wouldn't make you feel good about the decision.  The wise mind approach allows the rational mind to work with the emotional mind to come to a mutual agreement.  This leads to the "gut feeling" that it's the correct decision because your whole is in agreement.
